synthesis.problem: ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery times out at ClickHouse's 30-second max_execution_time while enumerating open-order addresses. ClickhouseQuery swallows the exception to an empty result, so scout:record-check-ins records zero check-ins; overlapping-cycle amplification belongs to DEV-2342.
synthesis.outcome: Remove the reported redundant address_links membership predicate without raising ClickHouse timeouts, preserve address enumeration semantics, and restore successful 15-minute-cached recorder cycles.

scope.summary: Limit DEV-2339 to the production-failing ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery. Leave the similar ScoutCheckInRollupQuery shape unchanged because its header explicitly documents the JOIN and IN as independently load-bearing.

proposed_changes.change: Remove `AND a.id IN (SELECT address_id FROM address_links)` after the existing INNER JOIN; retain all open-status, organization, staging, CDC-delete, geo-validation, direct-preference, and latest-version logic.
proposed_changes.reason: The ticket identifies duplicate membership evaluation as the timeout lead, while the JOIN already restricts results to address_links and carries hotlist_id/is_staged.

out_of_scope: DEV-2342: changing withoutOverlapping(10), schedule cadence, or lock-expiry behavior.
Raising max_execution_time globally or per query before fixing the query shape.
app/Clickhouse/Queries/ScoutCheckInRollupQuery.php: its JOIN carries is_staged and its IN predicate is explicitly documented as the primary-key pruning mechanism before bbox filtering.
CohortDeclinedQuery and CohortClosedQuery: their IN predicates constrain version aggregation to cohort IDs and are not address JOIN+membership duplicates.
Schema, index, CDC, materialized-view, or retention changes.

acceptance_criteria.item: ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery no longer exceeds ClickHouse's 30-second max_execution_time under the affected production-scale workload.

acceptance_criteria.reason: Timeouts currently degrade address enumeration to an empty array and produce zero check-ins.

acceptance_criteria.item: Address results remain one row per address, direct-preferred, with deterministic hotlist selection and coordinates from the latest CDC version.
acceptance_criteria.reason: These are existing downstream data contracts pinned by code and command tests.
The query should be corrected before relaxing the cluster safety limit.

acceptance_criteria.item: Keep the address cache TTL at 15 minutes.
acceptance_criteria.reason: ScoutRecordCheckIns::ADDRESS_CACHE_TTL_MINUTES is authoritative over the stale 30-minute ticket text.

acceptance_criteria.item: Do not modify ScoutCheckInRollupQuery as part of DEV-2339.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Its header explicitly says both predicates are load-bearing, it has bbox-specific behavior, and no timeout evidence was supplied for that query.
Concurrent-cycle amplification is tracked separately as DEV-2342.

questions.q: Does removing the membership predicate alone keep the largest affected org comfortably below 30 seconds on production-like ClickHouse data, despite public_address being keyed by id and the sibling query documenting IN as load-bearing pruning?

notes: ScoutRecordCheckIns caches each org's address enumeration for 15 minutes at app/Console/Commands/ScoutRecordCheckIns.php:42-47,180-188.
ClickhouseQuery catches production/testing exceptions and returns [] at app/Clickhouse/Queries/ClickhouseQuery.php:29-36, making timeout failures appear as empty address sets.
zod.public_hotlist_address is ORDER BY id, not hotlist_id, so its open-hotlist join remains intrinsically expensive.
The same exact JOIN+IN text appears only in ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery and ScoutCheckInRollupQuery.
No ClickHouse query or production data query was executed during this read-only fast pass.

tests.what_it_pins: End-to-end recorder semantics through ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery: Direct and Staging enumeration, shared-address direct preference, geo guards, caching, idempotency, radius matching, and graceful ClickHouse failure behavior.

Existing ScoutCheckInRollupQuery behavior if the sibling remains unchanged: Direct/Staging buckets, radius, hourly deduplication, kit/open/staging scoping, malformed geo handling, and short-plate exclusion.

grounding.code_flow: Scheduled scout:record-check-ins -> group Scout-enabled drivers by org -> ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery::query(cache:true, TTL 15m) -> on success, ScoutCheckInMatchQuery per kit over clarity.sc_positions -> PostgreSQL ScoutCheckIn::firstOrCreate; on a production ClickHouse timeout, ClickhouseQuery reports the exception and returns [], so the matcher short-circuits and records zero.

sites.reason: Reported production timeout site; ticket identifies the membership predicate as redundant after the same address_links JOIN.
The class header explicitly requires both: JOIN carries is_staged, while IN prunes public_address by its id key before bbox and geoDistance work.
IN limits hotlist version aggregation to cohort IDs; the outer JOIN applies scoped current-row attributes.

escalate.reason: The proposed removal follows the ticket lead and production symptom, but it conflicts with the sibling query's explicit statement that the same IN predicate is load-bearing for public_address primary-key pruning. Production-like EXPLAIN/timing is required before treating the one-line change as safe and sufficient.
